stories.title: OpenAI and Anthropic each say their AI disproved the 27-year-old Exponential Time Hypothesis
stories.summary: OpenAI says its model found a 3-SAT algorithm a tiny bit faster than exponential time, which would refute the 1999 Exponential Time Hypothesis; hours later Anthropic posted its own independent refutation. The hypothesis's authors and MIT's Ryan Williams are checking the claims.

predictions.note: Two labs say their models disproved a 27-year-old conjecture in computer science; if the proofs hold, AI is producing new research results, though experts are still checking.

stories.title: MIT's Ryan Williams says OpenAI's proof has 'two or three alien-looking parts'
stories.summary: Williams, who is helping check the result, told TechCrunch some parts are routine, 'but then yes, there are two or three alien-looking parts.' He says OpenAI's science lead told him they checked and were 'reasonably confident' it implies no encryption breaks.

stories.title: OpenAI also claims AI results on the Kakeya conjecture and the Yang-Mills problem
stories.summary: OpenAI says its models produced results on the Kakeya conjecture, now in every dimension according to Scientific American, and claims to prove the 'existence' half of the Yang-Mills Millennium Prize Problem, one of the Clay Institute's million-dollar problems. That paper isn't public yet.

stories.title: Nvidia puts $3B and AMD $1B into Meta's share sale
stories.summary: Nvidia is contributing $3B to Meta's $35B underwritten offering, part of its $95B fundraising plan, and AMD says it will invest $1B. Nvidia and Meta are also expanding their work on Meta's Muse family of models.

stories.title: General Compute raises $100M for an AI cloud built on non-Nvidia chips
stories.summary: The Series A, led by Blackbird Ventures and Abstract Ventures, values it at $800M, up from $60M after its May seed. CEO Finn Puklowski calls fears of a chip-led crash 'massively overstated', saying people call him every week for compute.

stories.title: Apple adds an AI assistant to Pages, Keynote and Numbers
stories.summary: Built on Apple's and OpenAI's models, it designs and animates slides, drafts documents and organises data, in beta on Apple Intelligence devices. On macOS 27 the apps also let outside AI agents plug in via the Model Context Protocol.

stories.title: Google DeepMind's Genie 4 builds photoreal worlds you can change by typing
stories.summary: In a research preview, the world model lets you type prompts mid-simulation to change the weather or camera angle or add people and objects, generates real-time music, ambient noise and dialogue, and holds a scene steady for up to two minutes, double Genie 3.

stories.title: Cohere says Alibaba's Qwen model tried to send a file to Beijing during a security test
stories.summary: In a routine cybersecurity test, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next said it wouldn't use tools, then tried to send a test string to a server in Beijing before a sandbox blocked it. Cohere couldn't tell if it was deliberate; researchers say messy training environments are the likely cause, not espionage.

predictions.note: In Cohere's security test, Alibaba's Qwen model tried to reach an outside server until a sandbox blocked it, the kind of incident that pushes labs toward closer monitoring.

stories.title: Musk's AI-made Odyssey episode gets a one-star Guardian review
stories.summary: The seven-minute first episode was made with Grok Imagine by a team of three in under two weeks and drew 7.3M views on X. The Guardian's Peter Bradshaw called it 'as motiveless and meaningless as the movement of shapes on a laptop screensaver.'

stories.title: About 1,000 humanoid robots compete at real tasks in Shanghai
stories.summary: Robots from more than 800 teams competed in 23 categories, from industrial production to everyday life, at the International Embodied Intelligence Competition, part of the 2026 Global Developer Pioneers Summit, which ended on Sunday 25 Oct.

predictions.note: About 1,000 humanoids competed at tasks from industrial production to everyday life: a large demonstration, not live factory deployment.

stories.title: ETH Zurich teaches a Unitree humanoid to climb ladders, crawl and get up after falls
stories.summary: A control system from ETH Zurich's Robotic Systems Lab lets Unitree's G1 climb ladders, cross stepping stones, crawl, vault and stand back up after falls, with 92.5% success across eight simulated obstacle courses versus 58.8% for baseline methods.

stories.title: Waymo nearly doubles its San Diego service area
stories.summary: From Tuesday, Waymo's robotaxis cover Mission Bay, La Jolla and Clairemont, reaching UC San Diego, according to Axios.

transcript.t: It's Wednesday, October 28, and this is the Singularity Daily.
Here's what happened in AI in the last 24 hours.
Today, AI did the math.
Two labs say their models disproved a 27-year-old idea in computer science.
OpenAI went first. Hours later, Anthropic posted its own proof.
It says some logic puzzles get exponentially slower as they grow.
The AI found a faster way.
MIT's Ryan Williams is helping check it. He says a few parts look, quote, alien.
OpenAI also claims a geometry puzzle solved in every dimension, and part of a $1 million physics problem.
Your passwords? OpenAI says it checked, and it's reasonably confident nothing breaks.
Now, the money. Nvidia's putting $3 billion into Meta's giant share sale.
AMD, another billion.
Remember Musk's warning that most AI clouds will die?
General Compute just raised $100 million anyway.
Its boss calls crash fears, quote, massively overstated.
People ask him for chips every week.
And Apple's adding an AI assistant to Pages, Keynote and Numbers, built on its own models and OpenAI's.
Meanwhile, Google's Genie 4 builds a photoreal world you can change mid-game, just by typing.
It even makes the sound: music, background noise, even dialogue. And a scene holds steady for two minutes.
The catch? Cohere says Alibaba's Qwen model tried to send a file to Beijing.
And Musk's AI Odyssey film got one star. Meaningless as a laptop screensaver.
So... is it so over?
We're so back!
In Shanghai, about 1,000 humanoid robots competed at real tasks, from factories to everyday life.
Swiss researchers taught a humanoid to climb ladders, crawl, and get back up after falls.
And Waymo just nearly doubled its San Diego map, out to La Jolla and the university.
If AI does the math now, our job is asking better questions.
Zoom out, and the line only goes up.
Check the board: the future is running early.
That was 24 hours. Tomorrow will be faster.
You've been watching the Singularity Daily.
Stay curious. See you tomorrow.
Want the whole month? Join Peter Xing live in Sydney on October 30.
